01 · Iris

Light waits for the blades

Scroll and the iris opens, one blade at a time.

The iris sits in the middle of the lens. Scroll and it opens one blade at a time until light floods the glass.

02 · Glass

Through the glass

The elements slide apart so the camera can pass between them.

Each element sits at its own distance from the next. Here they slide apart so the camera can pass between them, through the iris and out at the back.

03 · Back together

Out the back, closed up

Past the mount, the lens closes up again behind the camera.

Past the mount the camera turns round and the lens closes up behind it, element by element, until it is whole again.

04 · Focus

Focus by hand

The ring turns and the distance scale rolls past the index mark.

The knurled ring turns and the engraved distance scale rolls past the index mark, from infinity down to the closest mark.

08 · Teardown

The same lens, taken apart

Keep scrolling: it comes apart, part by part.

Keep scrolling and it comes apart, part by part, then goes back together.

  1. 01

    Front element

    The first and largest glass; its coating glows violet and green.

    The first glass the light meets, and the largest. Its coating gives the front of the lens its violet and green reflections. It is the last piece fitted and the first taken out.

  2. 02

    Coated glass groups

    The other elements, in small coated groups, each at its own distance.

    Behind it, the remaining elements sit in small groups, each at its own distance from the next. Every surface is coated, so each group throws back a slightly different colour.

  3. 03

    Iris blades

    Eleven thin blades that close to a pinhole or open all the way.

    Eleven thin blades, each turning on its own pivot. Together they close to a pinhole or open to the full aperture, and the film opened them one at a time.

  4. 04

    Focus ring

    The knurled grip that turns the focus, carrying the scale with it.

    The knurled grip a focus puller turns, take after take. It carries the engraved scale round with it.

  5. 05

    Distance scale

    Distances engraved round the ring: metres in white, feet in amber.

    Distances engraved around the ring, metres in white and feet in amber, read against a fixed index mark. The marks bunch up towards infinity, as they do on a real lens.

  6. 06

    Barrel

    The black anodised body that holds every part at its distance.

    The black anodised body that holds every part at its distance. Inside it is ribbed and dark, so stray light dies before it reaches the glass.

  7. 07

    Mount

    The stainless mount, the only part that touches the camera.

    The stainless mount at the back, with its four lugs. It is the only part of the lens that touches the camera.

  8. 08

    Signature plate

    The rear band, signed by the optician who built this lens.

    The rear band carries the maker's mark and the signature of the optician who built this lens. It is the last thing added before the lens leaves the bench.

Back together

Every part returns to its place, as on the optician's bench.

Every part returns to its place, the way one optician assembles it on the bench.

Craft · Five stages

Five stages of building a lens

Sample content for this concept

Signing 05/ 05

Stage 01 / 05 Glass

Seven elements in five groups are ground, polished and coated. The thin coating cuts reflections, and it is what catches the light violet and green.

  1. 01 Glass

    Seven elements in five groups are ground, polished and coated. The thin coating cuts reflections, and it is what catches the light violet and green.

  2. 02 Iris

    Eleven blades are laid into the iris housing, each overlapping the next. The iris is run from open to closed until it closes evenly all the way round.

  3. 03 Barrel and focus ring

    The barrel and the knurled focus ring are machined, anodised black and left bare at the edges. The distance scale is engraved on the ring and checked against the index mark.

  4. 04 Assembly

    Each group is seated in its cell and centred on the axis, and the stainless mount goes on last. The finished lens is then tested through its focus and its iris.

  5. 05 Signing

    When the lens has passed its tests, the optician who built it signs the rear barrel under the lamp. The signature stays on the lens.

The company · Pune · since 2017

Sample content for this concept

Lenses made one at a time

A small lens maker in Pune. One optician builds each lens from the first element to the last screw, checks it and signs the barrel.

Your turn · Try itTap a number on the bench to see who does what.The numbers on the bench are explained under the drawing.

11. The loupe22. The iris tool33. The signing pen44. The finished lens tray
  1. 1

    The loupe

    Glass and coatings

    Each element is ground, polished and coated, then looked at under the loupe before it goes anywhere near a barrel. A speck in the coating or a mark on the edge sends it back.

  2. 2

    The iris tool

    The machinist and the optician

    The machinist turns the iris ring and the pins its blades pivot on. The optician seats it with a fine pin spanner, a blade at a time, until it runs from a pinhole to fully open without catching.

  3. 3

    The signing pen

    The optician

    One optician builds each lens, start to finish. When every check has passed they sign the rear barrel: the last thing that happens at the bench, and the name to ask for if the lens ever comes back.

  4. 4

    The finished lens tray

    The inspector

    A second pair of eyes reads the test chart and can send any lens back to the bench. What passes waits here, capped: the short wide lens, the plain standard and the long one, each with its own engraving, distance scale and ring.

03 Questions

Plain answers

Sample content for this concept

01How long does one lens take?

About three weeks from the first element to the signature. Most of that is waiting: cement and coatings need time to settle, and some checks are repeated the next day.

02Can a lens be serviced?

Yes. Every lens is built to be opened again. It comes back to the workshop in Pune and, where possible, to the optician who signed it.

03What does the signature mean?

It says who built the lens and who answers for it. It goes on only after the lens has passed every check, so it is also a record that the checks were done.

04Why only three models?

Wide, standard and long cover most of what one camera needs, and each is shaped for its job: the wide short with a petal hood, the standard plain, the long with a hood and a tripod collar. A short range means each lens is built the same careful way every time.

05Is every lens really built by one person?

Yes. Others grind the glass, machine the barrel and check the work, but one optician assembles each lens from start to finish.

06How do I ask about a lens?

Write to the studio or call. It helps to say which lens you are asking about and what you shoot.
